html:
The Coast Yuki were a small Native people of the Mendocino coast of northern California, between Cape Vizcaino and the mouth of the Ten Mile River. They spoke a Yukian language related to that of the Yuki inland, a family found nowhere else.

They lived from the sea and the coastal forest: shellfish, seaweed, fish, sea lions, acorns and game. Their neighbours were the Northern Pomo to the south and the Wailaki to the north. After the California Gold Rush settlers seized the coast, and disease, killings and removal to the Round Valley reservation left very few Coast Yuki. Their language was extinct by the mid 1900s.
